_comment: The JTI fleet manifest: every deployable app, the folder it is REALLY built
from, and the Cloudflare Pages project it goes to. scripts/deploy.mjs reads
this file, so a correction here fixes the deploy for good instead of living
'verified' records how the folder -> project mapping was proven: the asset
hash in the local dist/index.html was compared against the one the live URL
serves. That is the only check that catches a deploy from a lookalike folder
(see notDeployed: 'TS GitHub' and the root-level quote app).

apps.name: JTI Unified Dashboard
notes: Registers a service worker: an open tab keeps serving the old bundle after a deploy. Hard-refresh (or Application > Service Workers > Unregister) before concluding a change did not ship.
public/_redirects must reach dist/ for SPA routing.

apps.name: CCW Issues (weigher visits)
notes: Its vitest run also covers ALL of shared/ (include: ../shared/**/*.test.{js,jsx}) plus media-worker.
media-worker has its OWN package.json (@anthropic-ai/sdk) — without `npm ci` in there too, rcu.test.js fails to import on a clean checkout even though it passes locally. Hence extraInstall.
The domain must stay in Firebase Auth > Settings > Authorized domains or login breaks.

apps.name: Headcount (multi-tenant CCW fork)
apps.verified: 2026-09-04 folder confirmed; live bundle is BEHIND the local dist
notes: Customer-facing. Live 2026-09-04 on index-CBZHfOyf.js while the local dist is index-C85LJFhn.js: there are built-but-undeployed changes here.

media-worker/ and redzone-worker/ in this folder are STALE FORKS of the CCW ones with the same worker names and missing modules. Never `wrangler deploy` from them: it would overwrite the production workers.

apps.name: Timesheet
notes: Build from `jti-timesheet`, NOT from `TS GitHub` — that folder is a stale variant whose bundle does not match production.

This folder is its OWN git repository nested inside DTLA and is git-ignored here, so DTLA's CI cannot see it. Its CI lives in jti-timesheet/.github/workflows/ci.yml and commits go from inside the folder.

apps.name: JTI Inventory (parts + boards)
notes: Shares the downtimelogger-a96fb Firebase project with CCW and MD Validation.

Has its own postcss.config.cjs so PostCSS stops searching at the app instead of picking up the repo-root config, which needs @tailwindcss/postcss from the ROOT node_modules. Without it the build fails anywhere the root install has not been run. Same for MD Validation.

apps.name: Metal Detection Validation
notes: Any new serving domain must be added to Firebase Auth > Settings > Authorized domains or sign-in fails with auth/unauthorized-domain.
Has its own postcss.config.cjs for the same reason as JTI Inventory: the repo-root PostCSS config would otherwise be found and demand @tailwindcss/postcss from the root node_modules.

apps.name: Service Quote builder
notes: There is a SECOND quote app at the repo root (root package.json, src/, dist/) with no login screen. Production is this folder, proven by hash. Do not deploy the root one by accident.
The old Netlify site jtiservicequote is stale.

apps.name: Shearers Downtime Logger
notes: The Cloudflare project is `jti-shearers`. `shearersjtidowntime` was the Netlify name and 404s here.
Used primarily on an iPhone — check the card view on a phone width.

apps.name: Parts diagram viewer (CUSTOMER)
notes: This is the customer-facing app. jti-ipm.netlify.app is a 301 forwarder to it.
Deploying PartsViewer/dist here would replace the customer app with the admin one — the project name is the only thing keeping them apart.

apps.name: Parts diagram admin
notes: Internal admin twin of jti-parts. Email/password sign-in; the domain needs to be in Firebase authorized domains.

apps.name: CCW history viewer (public share links)
notes: CCW Issues' SHARE_LINK_BASE_URL points at https://jti-ccw-viewer.pages.dev/view — share links customers already hold resolve here.

apps.name: CCW-R RCU training simulator
notes: jti-ccwr.pages.dev is a 301, not the app.
Deploy needs --branch main and an absolute dist path; this script always passes both.

apps.name: PDF service-report importer
notes: Sends parsed sheets to the Timesheet app's import_inbox. Sign-in needs jti-importer.pages.dev in Firebase authorized domains for timesheetapp-c4e54.

apps.name: CCW Centerline settings sheet
notes: Saved centerlines live in browser localStorage only — nothing is stored server-side.

apps.name: JTI Jobs Tracker
apps.verified: 2026-09-04 live 200; single-file app, no asset hashes to compare
notes: NOT a Vite app: the whole app is the hand-written single file JobsMASTER/dist/index.html. There is no build step.
JobsMASTER/functions/ is a Firebase Cloud Functions folder that wrangler mis-detects as Pages Functions and fails on. That is why the deploy runs from inside cf-jobs/, where wrangler cannot see it.
Its proxyStorage Cloud Function stays on Firebase/GCP and is unaffected by Pages deploys.

apps.name: Headcount customer guide
notes: No source folder in this repo — it is one self-contained HTML file, last kept at ~/Downloads/Headcount-how-to-use.html. Content is written from the Headcount CODE, not from public/USER_GUIDE.html.
Deliberately its own Pages project so publishing the guide never redeploys jti-issues-mt.
To publish: put index.html (+ a _headers with Cache-Control: no-store) in a folder and run `npx wrangler pages deploy <folder> --project-name=jti-headcount-guide --branch main`.

notDeployed.why: Stale timesheet variant. Production is the jti-timesheet folder — confirmed 2026-09-04: this folder's bundle hash does not match live.
A second, login-less copy of the quote app. Production is ServiceQuoteWA — confirmed by hash.
Local-only tool; its email corpus is mined from a PST and holds PII. Deliberately not published.
Local tool that turns scanned parts manuals into PartsViewer diagrams.
Dated snapshots of past app states; git-ignored and the only copies.
